reading.body:
The Genome Data Center is a research computing facility at Washington University in St. Louis supporting the McDonnell Genome Institute, which conducts large-scale DNA sequencing for cancer research and infectious disease genomics. The facility is real and currently operating, confirmed by the university's facilities management documentation, but the operator has not published specific IT megawattage capacity figures.

No power specification for this campus has been found in published sources. Without a published capacity figure, the facility cannot be ranked against other AI-relevant compute sites or assessed for its role in grid constraints on accelerator deployment.

Missouri has eight mapped data center facilities on record, but none in the state publishes megawatt figures. This campus therefore ranks first in Missouri only by virtue of being the sole facility there whose existence has been verified through operator documentation, not by size.
